speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower what are the specific challenges in ensuring that self-employed persons who provide delivery services on their own bicycles and personal mobility devices enjoy similar and adequate workplace safety protection as employees working for delivery companies, including insurance coverage in respect of injury, death and property claims arising from accidents while working.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: So, whether as employees or as SEPs, delivery riders on bicycles or personal mobility devices should have the proper equipment, protective gear and also sufficient training to ensure that they can do the job properly and safely.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This was announced by the Ministry in the Committee of Supply debate this year.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So, in our view, this is not the most prudent way of requiring companies to buy insurance for SEPs.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: However, there are other ways that the Workgroup is looking into now, for example, whether it would be useful for the SEPs themselves to buy the insurance since they are already in the service to provide services, programmes and activities to companies.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: As to third-party insurance claims, if a member of the public is injured by the employees of a company, then the third party can obviously take legal actions against the company for the injury that the third party sustains.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: But if the third party is injured by an SEP contracted by a company, then the situation is a little bit complicated.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: If the companies, the service buyers have not done this, then there is a reason for the Court to rule that the WSH Act was breached.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: However, if the company has taken all the necessary precautions, and it is solely the fault of the SEP, then the company is not liable for the SEP's actions.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Then the third party would have to take up the legal action against the SEP himself or herself.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Would the study group be looking into the possibility of making it mandatory for SEPs to have some form of third-party insurance?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: A second question would be: how long is this review likely to take?

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Yes, the Workgroup will look into various aspects.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So, we have to allow the Workgroup to consult all the tripartite partners and also the stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: When it is ready, we will make the announcement.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What I mean is basically that these companies should have hired them.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Instead, they purchased their services under this contract-for-service, therefore, making them self-employed.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So far as we know, we have not come across any cases of such disguised incidents.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: But if the Member should have any actual reports or information, I would appreciate it if he can let us know so that the Ministry will look into it.
